title: What If You Dipped Your Hand in Liquid Nitrogen? A Gas Shield Forms
subject: liquid nitrogen

scenes.text: What if you dipped your hand in liquid nitrogen? It would not freeze at once.
Liquid nitrogen boils at minus 195.8 Celsius. Your hand is 37, so it is far above its boiling point.
The skin boils a thin layer of the liquid into gas. That gas forms an insulating cushion between you and the liquid.
It is the Leidenfrost effect, the same trick that makes water drops skate across a hot pan.
But the shield is brief. Pull out in a fraction of a second, or frostbite sets in. If it soaks into clothing, it fails.
So the cold itself isn't the trap. The cushion is, because it only lasts a moment. Never try this.

description:
What if you dipped your hand into liquid nitrogen?
It boils at minus 195.8 Celsius, and your skin briefly sits on a cushion of gas called the Leidenfrost effect. It lasts only a fraction of a second.
